hero.paragraph: Hi, I'm Ny Hasina — a multidisciplinary creator passionate about technology, design, and bringing ideas to life.

webDev.title: Web Development
webDev.subtitle: Front-end developer specialized in crafting premium, responsive web experiences with React. Passionate about modern UI design, smooth interactions, and building visually distinctive interfaces with custom-made assets and icons.

gameDev.title: Game Development
gameDev.subtitle: Developing games has been a long-time passion of mine, and over the years I’ve built experience across every part of the process — gameplay programming, UI, tools, workflows, and asset creation. I enjoy crafting performant systems and creating efficient pipelines that accelerate development while maintaining a polished final experience.

lowLevelDev.subtitle: Low-level programmer specialized in C/C++, with strong foundations in memory management, optimization, and systems architecture. Experienced in rebuilding core Unix library components and developing performant software close to the hardware.

photoEditing.title: Photo Editing
photoEditing.subtitle: Comfortable with photo editing and visual asset refinement, with experience creating polished compositions and improving the overall presentation of a project.

3D.title: 3D
3D.subtitle: Passionate about 3D creation, I’ve built strong experience across nearly every part of the workflow using Blender — from modeling and texturing to rigging, animation, and environment creation. This versatility allows me to bring ideas to life while maintaining both creative control and technical consistency throughout production.

art.title: Art
art.subtitle: Because games are a blend of technology and art, I naturally became interested in the creative side of development as well. Even though I’m still continuously improving, I enjoy working on artistic aspects and developing my sense of composition, aesthetics, and visual storytelling.

multiMeshPainter.title: MultiMeshPainter
multiMeshPainter.content: <split>MultiMeshPainter is a custom editor tool I developed to bring an intuitive painting workflow to Godot's <link_multi_mesh_instance_3d>MultiMeshInstance3D</link_multi_mesh_instance_3d>, a feature that was missing from the engine but essential for my own game development.</split><split><line_break/>The tool enables artists and designers to paint, erase, and edit large numbers of instanced objects directly in the editor using a natural brush-based workflow while maintaining excellent performance, even with very dense scenes.</split><split><line_break/>To achieve this, I implemented a <bold>spatial hash</bold> that partitions instances into cells, allowing erase operations to inspect only nearby instances instead of the entire dataset. This reduces the average complexity to <bold>O(n<sub>local</sub>)</bold>, where <bold>n<sub>local</sub></bold> is the number of instances contained in the affected neighboring cells. Instance removal itself uses a <bold>swap-and-pop</bold> strategy, making buffer updates <bold>O(1)</bold> while avoiding unnecessary memory movement.</split><split><line_break/>The tool provides the flexibility expected from a professional foliage painting workflow. <newline/>It supports configurable <bold>random rotation</bold>, <bold>randomized scale</bold> within user-defined ranges, <bold>global instance scaling</bold>, <bold>per-instance color</bold>, and <bold>custom data</bold>. Color and custom data channels can be <bold>enabled</bold> or <bold>disabled</bold> at any time without invalidating or rebuilding existing instances, allowing users to adapt their <link_to_multi_mesh>MultiMesh</link_to_multi_mesh> configuration throughout production.</split><split><line_break/>Memory management is also built into the workflow. Users can freely grow the instance buffer while painting and shrink it back to fit the active instance count with a dedicated optimization command, keeping memory usage under control without affecting the scene.</split><split><line_break/><bold>PaintableMultiMesh</bold> remains fully compatible with Godot's native <link_multi_mesh_instance_3d>MultiMeshInstance3D</link_multi_mesh_instance_3d>. Users can seamlessly convert between editable and standard representations, making it possible to edit only when necessary while minimizing editor memory consumption.</split><split><line_break/>The project is implemented primarily in <bold>C++</bold> using <link_to_gdextension>Godot's GDExtension API</link_to_gdextension>, with the editor interface written in <bold>GDScript</bold>. It demonstrates custom editor tooling, performance-oriented algorithms, data-oriented programming, and engine-level integration.</split><split><line_break/>The addon is currently private while I continue refining it, with plans for a public release in the future.

schoolProjects.title: School Projects
schoolProjects.libft: Recreates basic C library functions and utilities from scratch.
schoolProjects.get_next_line: Implements a function to read a file one line at a time, focusing on buffers and memory management in C.
schoolProjects.ft_printf: Recreates the C printf function, teaching variadic functions, formatting, and type handling.
schoolProjects.philosopher: A multithreading simulation of the dining philosophers problem, focused on concurrency and synchronization.
schoolProjects.minishell: A simple Unix shell handling commands, pipes, redirections, and processes.
schoolProjects.webserv: A basic HTTP server built from scratch, covering sockets, HTTP, and server logic in C++.
schoolProjects.ft_transcendence: A full-stack project developing a real-time interactive real estate platform with an AI-powered search system, including end-to-end implementation of the user interface as well as backend and frontend functionality.
schoolProjects.ft_linear_regression: A small introduction to machine learning concepts through the implementation of a basic linear regression model and data visualization tools.

about.me: I'm a technology enthusiast and creator who enjoys bringing ideas to life through software, design, and digital art. Currently studying at <school>42 Antananarivo</school>, I have a strong interest in software development, game creation, and creative problem-solving. Beyond programming, I'm passionate about 3D art, visual design, and the artistic side of technology, always looking for ways to combine technical skills with creativity to build meaningful and engaging projects.
